newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN TO TIGHTEN BORDERS AGAINST SMUGGLING.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN TO TIGHTEN BORDERS AGAINST SMUGGLING.

text.p: The South African government said on Friday it has been advised to limit the clearing of commercial traffic into and out of the country to only 19 of its 52 border posts in a bid to control rampant smuggling that is threatening many industries and fueling crime.

Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi said that national and provincial ministers involved in the National Crime Prevention Strategy had also agreed that international cargo should be cleared at only eight of South Africa's 36 airports.
The recommendations will be presented to Cabinet next week.

Opening the debate on his 1997/98 budget vote in the national assembly, Mufamadi said that the 19 border posts and eight airports were being upgraded and re-organised to ensure proper control over all traffic.
"We have established much better integrated command structures, which are finalising strict procedures which must be followed at all land, air and sea points of entry and exit," Mufamadi said.

He said allowances would be made for local requirements under very strict controls, but emphasised that the bulk of commercial goods would be turned back from airports and border posts that had not been designated.
"Any international flights into or out of the country which do not register flight flow and which land and take off from unauthorised airports will be arrested," Mufamadi said.

"The aircraft will be seized and the pilots will be prosecuted. We will not allow the huge custom frauds and smuggling to continue, nor will we allow criminals to take stolen vehicles out and bring guns and drugs in."
